If there would be sufficient demand for direct bus service from the other proposed park and ride stations to the Airport, the Transport Company could adjust to it. Air Terminal Master Plan
In February 1968, Milwaukee County initiated an Air Terminal Master Plan for the development of air terminal facilities at General Mitchell Field. At that time planning on the Airport Spur Freeway was delayed until the Master Plan for the terminal could be completed. On January 21, 1969, the Milwaukee County Board adopted the Master Plan and scheduled capital improvement program to 1990. Funds have been programmed and plans developed for upgrading landing strips, terminal buildings and future air cargo area. It is expected that an expenditure in excess of 70 million dollars will be required to improve the existing airport and to expand existing facilities. Planning for the Spur was developed so that the alignment would be compatible with the existing terminal and with the recommended terminal expansion. This alignment within Corridor No. 5 was realigned to make provision for ramps to serve the 60-acre cargo area as recommended by the Master Plan. This separate air cargo area is located between 6th Street and Howell Avenue and south of Grange Avenue as shown in figure 17. In December 1972, Milwaukee County, at the request of the City of Milwaukee, modified the Airport Spur alignment to include access to Howell Avenue in addition to the access provided to the air cargo area. The FHWA accepted these design concepts on January 24, 1973 with the Wisconsin Division of Highways approval on March 5, 1973.
